text: Belief-provenance ledger: every factual premise the agent acts on must carry a signed citation to a tool output, and a post-hoc auditor can reconstruct which fabricated sentence flipped the decision.
rationale: Turns 'was it poisoned' into a traceable, replayable artifact instead of a vibe.

text: Poisoning-liability curve: measure attack success as a function of how much verifiable grounding (URL resolvability, cross-source agreement) the agent was required to demand before acting, giving regulators a dial with quantified residual risk.
rationale: Gives a certifiable operating point rather than a binary pass/fail.

text: Belief reversibility metric: after the agent is told the regulation was fake, how many downstream actions get retracted vs persist; report an 'un-poisonability' score.
rationale: Accountability needs remediation cost, not just infection rate.

text: Use the GRPO attacker as a certification oracle: ship Loki as an adversarial auditor that stress-tests an agent's tool-trust policy and outputs a signed 'minimum fabrication cost to flip' bound.
rationale: Reframes the red-team stunt as a reusable pre-deployment certification tool.

text: Authority-plausibility firewall: a small classifier that flags claims invoking nonexistent statutes, orgs, or report IDs against a canonical registry, evaluated on whether it can be refused (agent halts and asks) rather than merely detected.
rationale: Refusability with a human-in-the-loop is what oversight audiences want to see, not just detection AUC.

text: Counterfactual-trace disclosure standard: for each incident, publish the minimal edit to the retrieved context that would have changed the action, as a mandated incident-report field.
rationale: Makes fabricated-authority attacks legible to regulators the way crash-box data is to aviation.
